headline: Tabled decision on 1605 Sherman Avenue multi-unit housing project until September 2, 2026, on a 4-2 vote.
summary: Engineers and wetland scientists answered questions about stormwater, snow removal, lighting, and a vernal pool. Residents spoke for and against the project, and several written comments were also received. The public hearing was closed before the vote to table.
decisions: Tabled deliberations on the 1605 Sherman Avenue application to September 2, 2026, by a 4-2 vote.
Approved the July 1, 2026 meeting minutes as revised.

decision_evidence.quote: Commissioner McCollum moved to table deliberations of the application to the meeting of September 2, 2026. Commissioner Schneider seconded the motion. Commissioners McCollum, Schneider, Stone, and Shadle voted in favor; Commissioners Clapp and Laliberte were opposed. The item was tabled to September 2, 2026, with four in favor and two opposed.
Commissioner Clapp moved to approve the minutes of July 1, 2026, as revised. Commissioner Schneider seconded and all were in favor. The minutes were approved as revised.

plain_text:

Town of Hamden 
Planning and Zoning Department 
 
Inland Wetlands Commission 
Meeting Minutes 
 
Hamden Government Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel: (203) 287-7070 
Fax: (203) 287-7075 
 
August 12, 2026 
Revised August 25, 2026 
The Inland Wetlands Commission, Town of Hamden, held a hybrid Public Hearing and Regular 
Meeting on Wednesday, August 5, 2026. The meeting was held in-person in the Legislative Council 
Chambers at Hamden Memorial Town Hall, 2372 Whitney Avenue, Hamden, CT 06518, and 
remotely via Town Zoom teleconferencing at https://hamden.zoom.us/j/82474089466.  
 
Commissioners in Attendance: 
 
In Person: Michael Milazzo (Chairman), Michael Stone 
(Secretary), George Schneider, Jonathan Clapp, Deb 
Laliberte, Kirk Shadle 
Via Zoom: David McCollum (Vice Chairman) 
  
Staff in Attendance: In Person: Eugene Livshits (Town Planner), Thomas V ocelli, 
(Wetlands Agent), Tim Lee (Assistant Town Attorney), 
Maisie Albis (Commission Clerk) 
Via Zoom: Genevieve Bertolini (Stenographer) 
  
Chairman Milazzo called the meeting to order at 7:02p.m. Commissioner Stone called roll and 
established a quorum of six voting members.  
 
A. Public Comment Session 
 Chairman Milazzo called for comments from the public regarding topics within the purview of 
the Commission but not otherwise on the agenda. There were none from either in-person or virtual 
attendees.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
B. Application Review 
 1. IWC #26-1273—PUBLIC HEARING  CONTINUED FROM JULY 1, 2026 
1605 Sherman Avenue Received 05/06/2026 
Construction of a multi-unit residential development 
Applicant: 1605 Sherman Avenue LLC 
Attorney Bernard Pellegrino represented the application. He was joined by Mark Pucci, as 
well as Annette Ellis, George Logan, and Bill Kenny from the project team. Mr. Pellegrino first 
noted that the previous meeting had concluded with several questions posed to the applicant. He 
indicated that responses to most of those questions were included in materials submitted since
Page 2 of 6 Inland Wetlands Commission 8.5.26 Minutes 
 
July 1. He then acknowledged receipt of a letter from Matt Popp of Environmental Land 
Solutions on behalf of the neighbors opposed to the project. The questions and comments raised 
in that letter, he said, seemed to be referencing the previous iteration of the proposal. He felt that 
Mr. Popp’s questions had been adequately addressed by prior testimony. Mr. Pellegrino 
concluded his review of the hearing thus far and invited the Commission to ask questions of 
himself or the design professionals.  
Members had no initial questions. Engineer Annette Ellis came forward to elaborate on her 
responses to the questions from the previous meeting. Commissioner McCollum indicated that he 
had further questions based on those responses, but chose to reserve them until the other 
professionals had also presented.  
Commissioner Clapp asked why it was necessary for the snow removal plan to involve 
moving snow off-site. Ms. Ellis explained that the landscaping of the site did not allow enough 
area to pile snow during large storm events. She noted that the area designated for transported 
snow was still in the vicinity of a wetland, but offered that the upland review area could be 
demarcated with placards at regular intervals to prevent snow from being placed there. 
Commissioner Clapp then asked if the designated area would require tree clearing. Ms. Ellis 
replied that there would be some clearing in the 200-foot upland review area.  
There were no further questions for Ms. Ellis at this time. Registered soil and wetlands 
scientist George Logan presented next. Mr. Logan had submitted a supplemental response to 
questions raised at the previous meeting; he distributed copies of a vernal pool assessment sheet 
and ranking, per Calhoun and Klemens’ 2002 Best Development Practices (“BDP”), that he had 
referenced in that response. Based on his assessment, Mr. Logan determined that the vernal pool 
embedded in Wetland A would be rated Tier III. The BDP identifies Tier I and Tier II pools as 
vulnerable habitats for protection or restoration and recommends that best management practices 
be applied, he said, but does not do so for Tier III pools.  
Commissioner Shadle asked whether the classification of a vernal pool was static or dynamic 
over time. Mr. Logan reported that, with some exceptions, they remain fairly static. 
Commissioner Shadle then asked what the cutoff was for considering something to be a vernal 
pool rather than simply a seasonal accumulation of surface water. Mr. Logan stated that the 
determination would be based on the conditions of the surrounding watershed and upland review 
areas. 
Commissioner Shadle recalled that Mr. Logan had mentioned development in and around the 
area of a vernal pool leading to habitat degradation and asked that he describe that relationship 
further. Mr. Logan clarified that he had been referring to significant alterations of the landscape, 
such as the addition of new roads that fragment a habitat and affect migration patterns. 
Commissioner Shadle acknowledged that the post-development habitat would be large enough to 
support the existing populations. However, he noted that the proposal represented roughly a ten-
fold increase in density for that area and asked about the potential impacts of additional human 
activity. Mr. Logan said that the BDP considers the amount of intact terrestrial area being
Page 3 of 6 Inland Wetlands Commission 8.5.26 Minutes 
 
converted but does not address increases to density in already-developed areas. He asserted that 
the proposal does not significantly reduce the size of the habitat, does not alter hydrology, and 
improves water quality over existing conditions with enhanced stormwater management 
practices. 
Commissioner Shadle pressed Mr. Logan on whether it was his professional judgment that 
high density human activity has no impact on the ecological health of an area. Mr. Logan 
qualified his response: there is always a possibility that adding more human activity to an area 
could have measurable ecological impacts, but that is not the question before the Commission. 
Rather, he said, the Commission should be considering whether the proposal creates adverse 
physical impacts to the wetlands. 
Commissioner Stone referred back to the discussion of vernal pool tier classifications. He 
asked if Mr. Logan would expect any increase in biological activity or ecological value of the 
vernal pool in Wetland A as a result of heavy rain recently. Mr. Logan replied that he would not. 
He explained that an assessment of a vernal pool is based on its characteristics during the critical 
breeding period, and would not be readily impacted by isolated periods of increased rain. He and 
Commissioner Stone discussed how assessment incorporated both empirical observations and 
extrapolation based on professional experience. 
Commissioner Schneider briefly addressed Ms. Ellis to clarify that the area proposed for 
piling snow was on the applicant’s property. She confirmed, highlighting a portion of the property 
at the corner of Sherman Avenue and Kirk Road. 
Bill Kenny, professional wetland scientist, soil scientist, landscape architect, and principal of 
William Kenny Associates, presented next. He explained that his firm had primarily been 
providing landscaping services, but the applicant recently requested that they review the 
documentation that has been entered into the record thus far and assess the wetlands for potential 
impacts.  
Mr. Kenny reviewed the changes made to the landscaping and lighting plans since the 
previous meeting: the lighting plan was refined to be dark sky compliant; the landscape seed 
mixes were optimized; the stone-dust walking path was pulled out of the 100-foot buffer and 
placed closer to the building. He reported that he and another wetland scientist had visited the site 
for an inspection and reviewed the application materials to make a determination about potential 
impacts. They concluded that the proposal would not adversely affect the wetland, given that no 
work is proposed within the wetlands and the stormwater management practices are an 
improvement over existing conditions.  
Mr. Kenny agreed with Mr. Logan’s determination that the pool in Wetland A would be 
considered a Tier III vernal pool. He believed that the existing development in the area limited 
the potential for improvement to Tier II. He also reported that, according to Dr. Klemens, co-
author of the BDP, Tier III vernal pools do not require levels of protection beyond what would be 
provided to any other wetland.
Page 4 of 6 Inland Wetlands Commission 8.5.26 Minutes 
 
Commissioner Shadle asked if Mr. Kenny’s agreement with the Tier III ranking was based on 
his own personal inspection of the site. Mr. Kenny said that he considered his own observations 
as well as data provided by Mr. Logan and a review of the surrounding development. He and 
Commissioner Shadle further discussed the criteria by which he made his assessment, with Mr. 
Logan clarifying his assessment process as well.  
Chairman Milazzo called for additional questions from members. Hearing none, he asked Mr. 
Pellegrino if the applicant had anything else to present. Mr. Pellegrino replied that they had 
concluded their formal presentation. He added that closing remarks were prepared for the end of 
the hearing. 
Commissioner McCollum returned to the questions he had reserved during Ms. Ellis’ 
presentation. He asked the project team about the proposed lighting: whether the photometric 
plan accounted for the topography of the site; whether light may extend beyond the areas shown 
on the plan; whether lights would operate on timers or be motion-activated; and whether light 
pollution might have adverse impacts on the species associated with the vernal pool. He also 
asked what had prompted William Kenny Associates to produce a supplemental wetlands report. 
Mr. Kenny addressed each question. 
Commissioner McCollum then referred to the landscaping plan, noting that plant species were 
not identified for an area to the west of the building. He suggested that the applicant clarify the 
size, number, and species of trees to be planted there. He also asked about the duration of 
guaranteed replacement for failed plants and requested that the plan make reference to that 
guarantee.   
Commissioner McCollum directed his next series of questions to Ms. Ellis. He asked about 
the details for the amphibian exclusionary fence, which she identified on the plan. He then asked 
about the hydrological changes between the existing and proposed conditions. Ms. Ellis explained 
that the drainage areas would not be identical to existing conditions, but that the design would 
maintain or reduce flow rates and improve water quality. Commissioner McCollum asked how 
erosion would be controlled if rainwater were to exceed the capacity of the detention basin and 
flow past the emergency spillway. Ms. Ellis said that it would take an incredibly large storm event 
to create that situation but offered that erosion matting could be incorporated into the grass in that 
area for stabilization. 
Commissioner McCollum referenced a letter of testimony submitted by a citizen in opposition 
to the application which raised concerns about flooding on neighboring properties. He asked Ms. 
Ellis if the proposed conditions could lead to increased flooding. She reiterated that pre- and post-
construction flow rates would be equivalent. She added that the proposed stormwater 
management system would collect, control, and treat water more effectively than under existing 
conditions.  
Lastly, Commissioner McCollum asked Mr. Pellegrino if it would be feasible to structure the 
tenant lease to mandate that any dog waste from tenants’ guests be adequately collected, and 
include a monetary penalty for noncompliance. Mr. Pellegrino affirmed the possibility.
Page 5 of 6 Inland Wetlands Commission 8.5.26 Minutes 
 
Commissioner Shadle then referenced statements made by Mr. Logan regarding the 
jurisdiction of the Commission and asked Mr. Pellegrino if he agreed with and supported those 
statements from a legal perspective. Mr. Pellegrino confirmed. He cited a Connecticut Supreme 
Court case, Avalon Bay Communities v. Inland Wetlands Commission of the Town of Wilton. He 
reported that the court had found the Commission’s jurisdiction to be limited to impacts on the 
wetlands. 
With no further questions, the Chairman opened the floor to public testimony. A number of in-
person attendees commented on the application. Tisa Wegner, Marie Bravo, Brian Butler, Nick 
Hansen, Dana Parmalee-Guzman, and Jack Steveson spoke in support of the application. Megan 
Gruber, Lynn Orser, Kurt Bauknecht, Sandra Wright, Matt Popp, Vivian Cameron, Ken 
Ciardiello, John Pounds, Tom Ryan, and Tim Kerchoff spoke in opposition to it.  
Several written comments were received ahead of the meeting. Statements in support of the 
application were submitted by Alison Cunningham, Doug Foley, Emily Lopez, Katherine Foley, 
Marie Bravo, Nick Hansen, Petra Gardella, and Rita McCleary. Alison DiMaio, Steve and Megan 
Gruber, and the Elton Wetmore family submitted written comments opposing the application. 
Written testimony received between July 1 and August 5, 2026, is included in Appendix A. 
Property owner Mark Pucci came forward to explain his reasons for purchasing the property. 
He emphasized his commitment to protecting and restoring the wetlands on the site. 
Commissioner Schneider moved to close the public hearing on the item. Commissioner 
Clapp seconded and all voting members were in favor. The public hearing was closed.  
Commissioner McCollum moved to table deliberations of the application to the meeting 
of September 2, 2026. Commissioner Schneider seconded the motion. Commissioners 
McCollum, Schneider, Stone, and Shadle voted in favor; Commissioners Clapp and 
Laliberte were opposed. The item was tabled to September 2, 2026, with four in favor and 
two opposed. 
 
C. Old Business/New Business 
 
 
 
1. Review of July 1, 2026, Public Hearing and Regular Meeting minutes 
   Chairman Milazzo called for comments on the minutes. Commissioner Schneider noted that, 
on the fourth page, the name of a speaker who gave public comment regarding IWC #26-1273 
(1605 Sherman Avenue) should read “Emily Lopez” rather than “Emma Lopez.” The clerk noted 
the correction. 
Commissioner McCollum also referred to a name on the fourth page. He clarified whether 
William Neighbors was an individual person, with “Neighbors” being their last name. The clerk 
believed that was the case. While later amending the minutes, the clerk determined that the 
spelling of the last name should be “Nabors” and made that change accordingly.
Page 6 of 6 Inland Wetlands Commission 8.5.26 Minutes 
 
      With no further comments, the Chairman called for a motion. Commissioner Clapp 
moved to approve the minutes of July 1, 2026, as revised. Commissioner Schneider seconded 
and all were in favor. The minutes were approved as revised. 
 
2. Review site inspection schedule 
 Mr. V ocelli reported that there were no pending site inspections at this time. 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
3. Storm water catch-basin medallion update 
 Mr. V ocelli had nothing new to report regarding the medallions. He noted that he has reached 
out to individuals involved in the West Woods installation project but has not yet heard back. 
 
D. Adjournment 
 
 
 
 
 
      
 Chairman Milazzo called for a motion to adjourn. Commissioner Stone made the motion, 
seconded by Commissioner Schneider. All were in favor and the Chairman adjourned the 
meeting at 9:38p.m. 
 
 
 Submitted By: ______________________________ 
Maisie Albis, Commission Clerk

From Alison DeMaio <princessdemaio65@gmail.com>

CAUTION: This email originated from outside your organization. Exercise caution when opening attachments or clicking links,

        Dear Hamden Inland Wetlands                   Commissioners, 
Thank you for taking the time to read my  email.  
I am writing to provide a further clarification regarding the proposed
development at 1650 Sherman Avenue, specifically concerning snow
management practices and their relationship to the site's non‑permeable
surfaces.
As currently designed, the project includes substantial non‑permeable areas
—such as paved parking, driveways, and other hardscape surfaces—that will
accumulate snow mixed with road salt, sand, oils, and other contaminants
during winter maintenance. When stored on‑site, snow from these surfaces
will inevitably melt and flow downslope toward the adjacent wetland
uplands. This meltwater carries pollutants that can degrade water quality,
alter soil chemistry, and negatively impact vegetation and wildlife within the
regulated wetland area.
Because the site layout also presents sightline concerns for vehicles entering
and exiting the property, any attempt to keep snow piles away from traffic
visibility zones would push them closer to the wetland buffer. This creates a
direct conflict between public safety and environmental protection.
Given these constraints, I respectfully request that the Commission require
all snow originating from non‑permeable surfaces to be removed
off‑premise. Off‑site removal is the only reliable method to prevent
contaminated meltwater from entering the wetland system and to ensure
that snow piles do not obstruct critical traffic sightlines.
This requirement would provide clear environmental safeguards, maintain
safe roadway visibility, and ensure compliance with both wetland protection
standards and public safety considerations.
Thank you again for your continued attention to this matter and for your
stewardship of Hamden’s natural resources.
Sincerely, 
 Alison DeMaio
 70 Bear Path Rd


























Subject: IWC Application 26-1273 – 1605 Sherman Avenue 
Dear Chair and Members of the Inland Wetlands Commission, 
For the second time in two years, our basement has flooded. 
We have now experienced two major flooding events within an extremely short period of 
time. Events often described as rare or "once-in-a-century" no longer feel rare when your 
family has lived through them twice. 
We understand that the applicant's reports conclude the proposed stormwater systems 
will manage runoff. However, even the applicant's newest environmental assessment 
repeatedly states that those conclusions depend on the systems being properly installed, 
monitored, and maintained. 
That reliance on long-term maintenance is exactly what concerns us. 
The proposal increases impervious coverage on the site while relying on detention basins, 
engineered drainage systems, erosion controls, inspections, landscaping, and ongoing 
maintenance to protect the wetlands and surrounding neighborhood. 
One of the proposed snow storage areas is located directly across from our home. 
Throughout the winter, snow, road salt, sand, debris, and other pollutants from the parking 
areas will accumulate there. As temperatures rise and snow melts, that runoff will flow 
downhill through this connected watershed. 
As homeowners who have now cleaned up two flooded basements in two years, we cannot 
help but worry about what happens during the next major storm or rapid snowmelt. If our 
property floods again, we will be living with whatever runoff is moving through this system. 
That is not a hypothetical concern—it is our lived reality. 
The applicant believes the proposed infrastructure will improve existing conditions. But 
those conclusions depend on proper construction, ongoing inspections, sediment 
removal, repairs, vegetation management, and responsible maintenance for decades to 
come. 
As homeowners living immediately downhill from this site, including the proposed snow 
storage area, we are the people who will live with the consequences of this decision long 
after construction is complete. Based on our experience, we respectfully urge the 
Commission to deny this application and place the long-term protection of the wetlands 
and surrounding neighborhood first. 
Steve & Megan Gruber 
1700 Sherman Avenue
To whom it may concern, 
We are writing as a family members of the late Elton Wetmore and his son, 
Elton Lance Wetmore. As some may know, Elton lived at 660 Sheppard Ave 
for many years, and sold the land directly behind his home to the YMCA for 
the symbolic price of $1. He was an avid horseman and outdoor enthusiast 
who was pleased that the land would be used by the YMCA to allow others to
enjoy active lives. Both Elton and Lance passed their on love of the outdoors 
and active pursuits and their land and home on Sheppard Ave was the 
beginning of generations of horsemen. In their memory we hope that the 
YMCA parcel can continue to be used in a recreational capacity, or enjoyed by
another family, rather than being developed for mass residential use. 
Respectfully, 
• The Elton Wetmore Family
